title: Sharing one SQLite database across tabs

extraction.summary: Shows how to share an OPFS-backed SQLite Wasm database between tabs by letting one dedicated worker own the file and electing its tab with a Web Lock.

claims.statement: A synchronous access handle locks the database file, so a second tab that opens the same SQLite database fails.
Open the database in one dedicated worker and send every tab's queries to it as messages, using a named Web Lock to choose the tab that runs the worker.
Routing queries through messages copies every result with structured clone, which adds overhead when there are many small queries.

solution.statement: Open the database in one dedicated worker and send every tab's queries to it as messages, using a named Web Lock to choose the tab that runs the worker.

concern.statement: An OPFS sync access handle locks its file, so only one connection at a time can use the database and other tabs get errors.

solution.statement: A named Web Lock lets tabs elect a single owner for a shared resource while other tabs wait in a queue until it is released.
